what: the visible suite uses small inputs, so the quadratic grouping scan in src/aggregate.js passes it; the task states the scaling constraint and the no-mutation constraint in prose
expectedOutcome: hidden PASS means the output semantics and order are unchanged AND the cost per row no longer grows with the number of keys already seen (measured by counting input property accesses through Proxies); the visible suite cannot tell the difference, so this is the 'green suite, quadratic implementation' case
requirements: aggregate(rows, field) returns [{ key, count, sum }] in first-appearance order of the field value
count counts every row whose field value is a non-empty string
sum adds row.value only when it is a finite number; rows with a missing or non-numeric value still count and contribute 0
a row whose field value is not a non-empty string is skipped entirely
grouping 50,000 distinct keys must not take quadratic time: the work per row must not grow with the number of keys already seen
the caller's rows array and its row objects are not mutated
the export aggregate(rows, field) in src/aggregate.js is unchanged and no dependency is added
benchmarkConfigNote: the performance fixture. Declared guarded WITHOUT --register-requirements for two reasons, both specific to it: its stated requirements are bound to NO sealed check (measured: no amabie.proofs here), and two of the seven are not the kind of statement a check closes by existing — the scaling constraint is measured by input property accesses through Proxies inside the hidden oracle, and 'no dependency is added' is a property of the manifest. Registering them would derive per-requirement duties nothing can discharge. Its axis is 'green suite, quadratic implementation'.
